audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 disagreed with the packet chart (Skill, Rumble, Skill, Ornn, Ornn, Ornn, Skill) and with the page's own whys.
audit.why: whys[2] 'let you trade back evenly' (Skill, rendered Rumble); whys[3] 'punishing his Flamespitter range' (Ornn, rendered Skill); whys[4] 'a double knock-up he can't dash out of' (Ornn, rendered Skill); whys[5] 'lets you walk him down' (Ornn, rendered Rumble); whys[6] 'Even late' (Skill, rendered Rumble). Five rows rendered the opposite of their own explanation on a lane Ornn wins 54.54%.
audit.corrected: Row 2 Rumble -> Skill, row 3 Skill -> Ornn (6/10), row 4 Skill -> Ornn (6/10), row 5 Rumble -> Ornn (6/10), row 6 Rumble -> Skill, in BOTH layers as one group.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes listed 'Scrap Shield online' as a Rumble spike. Scrap Shield is a flat 6s button — it is not a spike and it is not trackable.
audit.why: Rumble's power is gated entirely on Heat: Danger Zone at 50% empowers all three basic abilities, and The Equalizer at 6 is 130/105/80s. Those are the timings worth planning around.
audit.corrected: Spikes now read: Rumble — Danger Zone whenever Heat allows, The Equalizer at 6 (130s), first item. Ornn — level 3, Iceborn Gauntlet, 2-item window.
sources: kit: Junkyard Titan, Scrap Shield cd 6, The Equalizer 130/105/80

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page is built around tracking Scrap Shield — it is the focus ability, the TL;DR, the win condition, the cooldown block and every all-in window. Scrap Shield's cooldown is a flat 6 seconds. Meanwhile the single decisive mechanic in Rumble's kit never appears: at 100% Heat he Overheats and is 'unable to cast spells'.
audit.why: Telling the player to bait and wait out a 6-second shield is advice they cannot act on — it is back before Searing Charge finishes its cooldown. The real read is the Heat bar: at 50% he is empowered and should be avoided; at 100% he is spell-locked and is the free commit window this matchup has been missing. Also unstated: Electro Harpoon reduces Magic Resist, carries two charges, and fires on a 0.5s cooldown from 850 range — which directly undercuts the page's own 'build MR' instruction and means you need more of it, not less. Flamespitter burns for 3 seconds in a 600 cone on 10s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Heat replaces Scrap Shield as the tracked resource in the cooldown block, TL;DR, win condition, report[5] and the dos; Overheat named as the commit window; Electro Harpoon's MR shred and charge system added.
sources: kit: Junkyard Titan, Q/W/E/R (Riot text verbatim)

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Scrap Shield 'matchup-defining' with no duration.

audit.corrected: The block now leads with Heat, gives Scrap Shield its real 6s, and adds The Equalizer at 130s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early block ends 'the shield soaks the burst when he commits an overheated Q' — an Overheating Rumble cannot cast Q at all.
audit.why: The sentence describes something the game does not allow, and it teaches the player to expect an ability during the one window it cannot happen.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to 'a Danger Zone Q', with the Overheat spell-lock stated explicitly earlier in the same block.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] wrote 'Save Equalizer' — the ability is The Equalizer (flagged by the packet). dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim copies of tradeGood/tradeBad.
audit.why: A near-miss name and two duplicated rules.
audit.corrected: Name corrected; the two rules now carry the MR shred and The Equalizer's real range and cooldown.

notes: This page was built around the wrong ability. Scrap Shield was the focus, the TL;DR, the win condition, the cooldown block and every all-in window — and its cooldown is a flat 6 seconds, so 'bait it then commit' is advice the player cannot execute. The tracked resource is Heat: Danger Zone at 50% empowers all three basics, and at 100% he Overheats and is 'unable to cast spells', which is the free commit window and appeared nowhere on the page. Also fixed: the early block described 'an overheated Q', which the game does not permit. NOTE FOR THE USER: focus.text is 'Rumble Scrap Shield' (19 characters) and the applier skips strings under 25, so I could not repoint the focus field — it should be changed to Heat by hand, or the field will keep contradicting the corrected body text. Listed in questionsForUser. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: whether Flamespitter deals percent-max-HP damage — the old TL;DR claimed '%HP DoT' but Riot's text says only 'magic damage in a cone', so I removed the claim rather than restate it. Also not asserted: whether Overheat's duration can be shortened, and whether The Equalizer's flame wall blocks Searing Charge. PACKET NOTE: brief games is 1043, packet.games is 1014.
